title: The nations' foreshadows — seeds of the Word, fulfilled in Christ
body: Every faith of the nations that came before Christ, credited MAGNANIMOUSLY where it contributed positively and read as a foreshadow — the seeds of the Word scattered among the peoples (Acts 17), the shadow whose substance is Christ (Colossians 2:17), the true Light refracted (John 1:9). We honor the seed and name the fulfillment plainly, for we do not hide the light. What arose after Christ is measured by the test of the spirits — whether it confesses or denies the Son come in the flesh (1 John 4:2-3) — carried as Matt's framing, anchored on the text, and held always in love: the door to the fulfillment stands open to all. 'We don't lie, but we love you.'

title: Praeparatio evangelica — the foreshadow and the fulfillment
body: The principle beneath this whole shelf: God did not leave the nations without witness (Acts 14:17). He wrote his law on every heart (Romans 2:14-15), showed his power in what is made (Romans 1:19-20), and set the times and places of the nations 'that they should seek God, and perhaps feel their way toward him' (Acts 17:26-27). So among the peoples he scattered SEEDS of the Word (Justin Martyr's logos spermatikos) and SHADOWS of the thing to come (Colossians 2:16-17) — the true Light that enlightens everyone (John 1:9) breaking in refracted. We honor the seed and the shadow generously; and because a shadow exists only where a body casts it, we name the Body plainly. We do not hide the fulfillment for fear of the light — that would be to love the shadow more than the One who cast it.

title: The test of the spirits — 1 John 4:2-3 (held in love)
body: The calibration for what came AFTER Christ, carried as Matt's framing and anchored on the text: 'By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God, and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God. This is the spirit of the antichrist' (1 John 4:2-3; cf. 2:22, 'the liar is the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ'; 2 John 7). The foreshadows PREPARED for the Son; a teaching that arises after him and DENIES the Son — his incarnation, his death, his deity — is, by this test, of the antichrist spirit. Three guardrails, kept strictly: (1) the test is of SPIRITS and TEACHINGS, never of persons or peoples — we love every soul and condemn none; (2) it is stated with grief, not triumph — 'we don't lie, but we love you'; (3) the door stands open — the invitation is always toward the Son the shadow was pointing at all along.

title: Israel and the Hebrew Scriptures — not a shadow but the root and the promise
body: Set apart from the foreshadows in kind, and honored above them: the covenant with Abraham, the Law and the Prophets are not a distant shadow among the nations but the very ROOT and PROMISE — the cultivated olive tree onto which the nations were grafted (Romans 11:17-24). To Israel belong 'the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the worship, and the promises' (Romans 9:4-5); they were entrusted with the very oracles of God (Romans 3:2). Every foreshadow elsewhere is dim; here the light is direct — 'beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, he interpreted... the things concerning himself' (Luke 24:27). We hold this people and this Scripture with the deepest honor, and the fulfillment we name is not a rival but the homecoming the Prophets themselves foretold — Messiah, the consolation of Israel (Luke 2:25-32).

title: Greek philosophy (Platonism & the unmoved mover)
body: Greek philosophy (Platonism & the unmoved mover) (c. 6th–4th c. BC). The seed it kept: the intuition of a transcendent Good, the eternal Forms behind appearances, a divine Reason (logos) ordering all things, and an 'unknown god' beyond the idols (Acts 17:23). Where the shadow fell short: its God was impersonal and its Logos a principle, never a Person; it reasoned toward the divine but could not be reconciled to it. The fulfillment (named, not hidden — we do not fear the light): 'In the beginning was the Logos, and the Logos was with God, and the Logos was God... and the Logos became flesh' (John 1:1,14) — the principle the philosophers glimpsed is a Person who came. (Credited in love as a foreshadow — praeparatio evangelica, Acts 17:23; the shadow whose substance is Christ, Colossians 2:17.)

title: Stoicism
body: Stoicism (c. 3rd c. BC onward). The seed it kept: conscience and natural law, a providence governing all, the divine logos indwelling the world, and the brotherhood of all humanity — Paul quotes their poets: 'in him we live and move and have our being... for we are indeed his offspring' (Acts 17:28). Where the shadow fell short: it made the logos pantheistic and impersonal, and sought salvation in self-sufficiency and detachment rather than in grace and love. The fulfillment (named, not hidden — we do not fear the light): the law written on the heart (Romans 2:15) is fulfilled by the Spirit given, not the will steeled; the offspring the Stoics named can become sons by adoption (Galatians 4:5). (Credited in love as a foreshadow — praeparatio evangelica, Acts 17:23; the shadow whose substance is Christ, Colossians 2:17.)

title: Zoroastrianism
body: Zoroastrianism (c. 1200–600 BC). The seed it kept: one wise Lord (Ahura Mazda), a real moral struggle of good against evil, a coming Savior (Saoshyant), the resurrection of the body and a final judgment — and the Magi who read the heavens and came to worship the newborn King (Matthew 2:1-11). Where the shadow fell short: it framed the struggle as a dualism of two near-coequal principles, rather than one sovereign God over a defeated evil. The fulfillment (named, not hidden — we do not fear the light): the awaited Savior came, the resurrection it hoped for was accomplished first-fruits in Christ (1 Corinthians 15:20-23), and its own wise men were led to the manger. (Credited in love as a foreshadow — praeparatio evangelica, Acts 17:23; the shadow whose substance is Christ, Colossians 2:17.)

title: Ancient Egyptian religion (Ma'at)
body: Ancient Egyptian religion (Ma'at) (c. 3000–30 BC). The seed it kept: Ma'at — truth, justice and cosmic order as the will of heaven — and a vivid expectation of judgment after death, the heart weighed against the feather of truth. Where the shadow fell short: it scattered the one order among many gods and trusted in spells and magic to pass the judgment. The fulfillment (named, not hidden — we do not fear the light): there is a judgment, and a heart no spell can make light — but 'there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus' (Romans 8:1), whose righteousness is credited, not weighed and found wanting. (Credited in love as a foreshadow — praeparatio evangelica, Acts 17:23; the shadow whose substance is Christ, Colossians 2:17.)

title: Mesopotamian religion (Sumer, Babylon)
body: Mesopotamian religion (Sumer, Babylon) (c. 3000–500 BC). The seed it kept: the earliest written law codes binding a people to justice, a keen sense of cosmic order, and a preserved memory of the great Flood carried in its epics. Where the shadow fell short: its gods were capricious and quarreling, and its Flood was remembered as myth, its true shape distorted. The fulfillment (named, not hidden — we do not fear the light): the Law finds its ground not in a king's stele but in the God who gives it (Exodus 20), and the Flood it half-remembered is told true in Genesis 6-9 — with a covenant and a bow of mercy in the cloud. (Credited in love as a foreshadow — praeparatio evangelica, Acts 17:23; the shadow whose substance is Christ, Colossians 2:17.)

title: Vedic religion and early Hinduism
body: Vedic religion and early Hinduism (c. 1500 BC onward). The seed it kept: rita, the cosmic moral order; sacrifice placed at the very center of worship; and a deep, unquenched hunger for union with the divine and the unseen. Where the shadow fell short: it dissolved the personal Creator into an impersonal Absolute and set the soul on endless cycles of rebirth to be escaped, not a body to be raised. The fulfillment (named, not hidden — we do not fear the light): the sacrifice the altars reached toward is offered once for all in Christ (Hebrews 10:10), and the hunger for the divine is met not by absorption but by adoption — 'that they may be one, as we are one' (John 17:22). (Credited in love as a foreshadow — praeparatio evangelica, Acts 17:23; the shadow whose substance is Christ, Colossians 2:17.)

title: Buddhism
body: Buddhism (c. 5th c. BC). The seed it kept: an unflinching diagnosis of the human condition — that life as we grasp it is shot through with suffering (dukkha) — profound compassion, and a refusal to rest in the emptiness of created idols. Where the shadow fell short: it found no personal God to cry to and no Redeemer to send, and set the goal as the extinction of the self (nirvana) rather than communion with the Living One. The fulfillment (named, not hidden — we do not fear the light): the suffering it named so honestly is real (Romans 8:20-22), but the answer is not to be blown out like a candle — it is a Man of Sorrows who bore it (Isaiah 53:3-4) and a self not annihilated but raised. (Credited in love as a foreshadow — praeparatio evangelica, Acts 17:23; the shadow whose substance is Christ, Colossians 2:17.)

title: Chinese traditions — Confucianism & Daoism
body: Chinese traditions — Confucianism & Daoism (c. 6th–5th c. BC). The seed it kept: the moral order and the cultivation of virtue, filial reverence, the rectification of names — and, in Daoism, 'the Way' (the Dao): an ineffable Source from which all things flow, and the wisdom of yielding (wu wei). Where the shadow fell short: the moral order had no covenant-keeping Person behind it, and the Way was a principle, nameless and impersonal, never a Someone who could be known or followed home. The fulfillment (named, not hidden — we do not fear the light): 'I am the Way' (John 14:6) — the Dao the sages reached toward has a face and a name; the order written on the heart is kept by the One who wrote it and now indwells. (Credited in love as a foreshadow — praeparatio evangelica, Acts 17:23; the shadow whose substance is Christ, Colossians 2:17.)

title: The dying-and-rising motif in the mysteries
body: The dying-and-rising motif in the mysteries (antiquity). The seed it kept: the deep, near-universal human intuition — carried in Osiris, Dionysus, Tammuz and others — that life is somehow won through death, and that a god might die and live again. Where the shadow fell short: these were myths without a date, a place, or a witness — seasonal dreams, not events; they longed for what they could not make true. The fulfillment (named, not hidden — we do not fear the light): the pattern every culture dreamed became FACT in one place at one hour — 'the true myth' (C.S. Lewis): crucified under Pontius Pilate, raised the third day, seen by five hundred at once (1 Corinthians 15:4-6). The shadows dreamed it; Christ did it. (Credited in love as a foreshadow — praeparatio evangelica, Acts 17:23; the shadow whose substance is Christ, Colossians 2:17.)

title: Primal religion and the 'unknown god'
body: Primal religion and the 'unknown god' (all ages). The seed it kept: the near-universal witness of conscience, the awe before creation, and the reaching-after of every people 'in the hope that they might feel their way toward him and find him' (Acts 17:27) — the altar to the unknown god on every hill. Where the shadow fell short: left to itself it slid toward idols, exchanging the glory of the immortal God for images (Romans 1:23), feeling after a God it could not name. The fulfillment (named, not hidden — we do not fear the light): 'What therefore you worship as unknown, this I proclaim to you' (Acts 17:23) — the God felt-after in the dark has drawn near and made himself known in his Son. (Credited in love as a foreshadow — praeparatio evangelica, Acts 17:23; the shadow whose substance is Christ, Colossians 2:17.)

title: Islam under the test of the spirits (Matt's framing, anchored, in love)
body: Credited where it contributes positively: a strict and serious monotheism, a deep reverence before God, moral earnestness, the honoring of many prophets, and a call to prayer and mercy. And then, held to the one test in love: arising in the 7th century AD, after Christ, it explicitly denies the crucifixion ('they did not kill him... but it was made to appear so to them', Qur'an 4:157) and denies the Sonship and deity of Christ (Surah 112; 5:72-75) — which is precisely the confession that 1 John 4:2-3 and 1 John 2:22 make the dividing line. So by Matt's framing, carried faithfully, a teaching that denies the Son come in the flesh bears the antichrist spirit named in that test. This is said of the DOCTRINE'S denial, never of any Muslim soul — every one of whom is loved, and for whom the door to the fulfillment stands wide open. 'We don't lie, but we love you': the cross the Qur'an calls an appearance is the very place the love of God was proven (Romans 5:8).

title: The pattern for movements arising after Christ (the test, in love)
body: Beyond any single case, the calibration is a pattern, applied gently: a religion or movement that arises AFTER Christ and redefines, demotes, or denies the Son — his full deity, his incarnation, his atoning death and resurrection — falls under the test of 1 John 4:2-3, whatever real goods it also carries (community, discipline, moral seriousness). We name the denial honestly and credit the goods generously; we never pronounce on the standing of any person before God, which is his alone to judge (Romans 14:4). The foreshadows before Christ ache toward him; a teaching after him is measured by whether it confesses him. In both directions the compass points to one place, and the invitation is the same: come to the Son.
